Rule: "When standard-decimal or standard-binary arithmetic is in effect, each arithmetic statement is defined in terms of one or more arithmetic expressions. Unless specified otherwise in rules, transfer of data from an intermediate form into a resultant-identifier shall be according to the specifications in 14.6.8" + NOTE 1 "The ROUNDED phrase applies only to this transfer of data." cite.py --check 14.7.7 "When standard-decimal or standard-binary arithmetic is in effect, each arithmetic statement is defined in terms of one or more arithmetic expressions" -> OK §14.7.7 3). TWO-PART rule. STANDARD-DECIMAL half (claimed) VERIFIED by probe @0caa7d5 with OPTIONS ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL at --std 2014 and 2023 (identical): COMPUTE X ROUNDED = 2 / 3 * 3 (S9V9) -> +2.0 (ROUNDED applied to the final transfer only; per-step rounding would give 2.1); COMPUTE Y = 2/3*3 -> +2.0; COMPUTE Z ROUNDED = 1/3 + 1/3 (S99V99) -> 0.67; ADD 0.05 TO N ROUNDED (1.2 -> 1.3, default NEAREST-AWAY-FROM-ZERO); ROUNDED 0.25 -> 0.3 and -0.25 -> -0.3; COMPUTE W(PIC 9) = 12.7 -> SIZE ERROR, W unchanged (NOTE 2, size error on transfer); W = -3.9 -> 3 (unsigned receiver, fraction truncated, §14.6.8); MULTIPLY 1.15 BY X Y ROUNDED -> X 2.3 (unrounded), Y -0.345 -> -0.3 (only the ROUNDED receiver rounds). Code: NumericRenderer.StandardDecimal routes the evaluation through the decimal engine and the store goes through ReceivingStore / RuntimeApi.NumStoreRounded, the §14.6.8 transfer. STANDARD-BINARY half: declined — OptionsBinder raises COBOLNET0806 for ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY (docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 2, Not claimed — REVISITABLE; kb/Work PB198), so that half is unreachable. No spec-derived test pins the standard-decimal ROUNDED-only-on-transfer behaviour (test-needed). Whether a row half-covered by a declined element closes CONFORMS on its claimed half or carries DNS is the open owner question kb/Work PB1151 (b), which names GR-14.7.7-3. NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION.
